concepts.title: Meaning and Many Views of Work

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Many Views of Work' refers to.
questions.a: Purposeful human effort, paid or unpaid, through which a person earns a living, uses personal talent, builds relations and finds a place in society.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Many Views of Work'.
questions.a: Work is more than wages: it shapes identity, dignity and contribution to family, employer and society.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Meaning and Many Views of Work', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- work can be seen as job, duty, dharma, calling or self development

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaningful Work' refers to.
questions.a: Effort that helps society or others, is carried out responsibly, is enjoyed by the worker, and leaves room to apply skill, judgment and creativity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaningful Work'.
questions.a: Meaningful effort repays the worker with growth, confidence, self worth and recognition.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Meaningful Work', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- usefulness plus responsibility plus enjoyment makes effort meaningful

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Job versus Career' refers to.
questions.a: A job is engagement in work mainly for earnings, while a career is a sustained climb inside one chosen field, powered by the wish to grow and excel.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Job versus Career'.
questions.a: A career needs continual upgrading of skills and knowledge, not just appointment to a post.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Job versus Career', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative contrast -- job pays now, career builds over a lifetime

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Livelihood and Career Management' refers to.
questions.a: Livelihood is the occupation and means through which a person meets basic needs, while a career is the lifelong, evolving sequence of roles each individual manages.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Livelihood and Career Management'.
questions.a: Careers are unique and dynamic; managing one means making transitions whenever needed.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Livelihood and Career Management', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- career growth means balancing paid work, learning and life roles

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Traditional Occupations of India' refers to.
questions.a: Farming, fishing, weaving, handicrafts, regional cuisines and visual arts carried across generations form the inherited occupational base of Indian villages, once passed on as guarded home training.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Traditional Occupations of India'.
questions.a: Mass produced goods, poor finance and weak marketing now squeeze artisan incomes, so revival needs design, training and IPR protection.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Traditional Occupations of India', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- inherited craft skill sustained rural livelihood for centuries

concepts.title: Gender, Sex and Women and Work

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Gender, Sex and Women and Work' refers to.
questions.a: Sex sorts people by biology and chromosomes; gender is the social identity and the set of expected roles a culture attaches to being male, female or third gender.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Gender, Sex and Women and Work'.
questions.a: Household work done by women is a real economic contribution and must be valued like paid work; working women also carry a double burden of job plus home care.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Gender, Sex and Women and Work', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative contrast -- sex is biological, gender is socially built

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Quality of Work Life' refers to.
questions.a: Quality of Work Life is the degree to which a workplace meets the social and psychological needs of employees alongside economic ones, treating people as assets rather than costs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Quality of Work Life'.
questions.a: Job satisfaction flows more from attitude, fair comparison and growth chances than from pay alone.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Quality of Work Life', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- fair treatment plus participation plus balance lifts morale and output

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Life Skills for Livelihood' refers to.
questions.a: Practical abilities for adaptive, positive conduct that let people handle everyday demands; experts list ten core sets, from self-awareness and empathy through to coping with emotions and stress.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Life Skills for Livelihood'.
questions.a: Life skills protect health and well being across the lifespan and grow through experience, not lectures.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Life Skills for Livelihood', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: knowledge plus attitudes plus values lead to life skills and psychosocial competence

concepts.title: Dignity of Labour, Values and Ethics

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dignity of Labour, Values and Ethics' refers to.
questions.a: Taking pride in every kind of honest effort is the dignity of labour; values are personal beliefs about what is good, while ethics are rule systems that a profession formally adopts.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dignity of Labour, Values and Ethics'.
questions.a: Ethical behaviour cuts waste, lifts morale and raises productivity for everyone around.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Dignity of Labour, Values and Ethics', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- respect for every worker plus ethical conduct sustains a workplace

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Ergonomics at the Workplace' refers to.
questions.a: Built from Greek roots for work and natural laws, ergonomics studies people on the job and reshapes tools, workstations and methods so the workplace fits the worker instead of the reverse.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ergonomics at the Workplace'.
questions.a: Anthropometry, biomechanics, physiology and industrial psychology are its four pillars; good design cuts injuries, errors and absenteeism.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Ergonomics at the Workplace', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: goal -- adapt work environment to worker for safety, comfort and productivity

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Entrepreneurship and the Entrepreneur' refers to.
questions.a: The act of building a fresh enterprise, product or service by organising resources and finances and by taking calculated risks to turn a novel idea into reality.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Entrepreneurship and the Entrepreneur'.
questions.a: Social entrepreneurs chase large scale social benefit and measure success by impact, not profit.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Entrepreneurship and the Entrepreneur', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: qualitative idea -- entrepreneur equals innovator plus organiser plus risk taker

concepts.title: Creche Rule of the Factories Act

questions.q: How many workers above thirty must an industry have before a creche becomes compulsory? Use the method 'Creche Rule of the Factories Act'. Work with: women_employed = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of women_above_limit.
questions.a: 270 units

questions.q: Find the excess over the creche trigger when an industrial unit reports W women on its rolls. Use the method 'Creche Rule of the Factories Act'. Work with: women_employed = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of women_above_limit.
questions.a: 50 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Creche Rule of the Factories Act' refers to.
questions.a: Under Section 48 of the Factories Act, an industry that keeps more than thirty women on its rolls must run a creche for children under age six.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Creche Rule of the Factories Act'.
questions.a: A positive excess over the thirty woman mark means the factory has crossed the creche trigger.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Creche Rule of the Factories Act', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: women_above_limit = women_employed - 30

concepts.title: Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise

questions.q: How much annual business does each member bring in when total sales of T crores are shared by M members? Use the method 'Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise'. Work with: current_members = 512, turnover_crores = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of per_member_sales.
questions.a: 9765625 units

questions.q: Compute the per head sales value in rupees for a self employment society that logs S crores with N members. Use the method 'Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise'. Work with: current_members = 4096, turnover_crores = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of per_member_sales.
Explain in your own words what 'Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise' refers to.
questions.a: When a women's collective reports its sales in crores, each member's share of the business can be found by converting the turnover to rupees and dividing it across the whole membership.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise'.
questions.a: One crore carries one crore rupees, so scale the turnover before dividing by members.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Turnover Sharing in a Women's Enterprise', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: per_member_sales = turnover_crores * 10000000 / current_members
